headline: Fed's hawkish hold fails to lift the dollar; loonie firms on BoC hike, won and rupiah slide
summary: The dollar index slipped about 0.2% to near 102.15 after the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with two dissents for a hike, because the curve steepened during Warsh's press conference and a December hike (about 85%) was already priced. The euro and loonie led, up about 0.3–0.4%, while the won fell 1% in Seoul on short covering and the rupiah closed at a record low.
drivers: A hawkish Fed hold, priced already

The Fed upgraded growth to "strong", kept inflation "elevated", and Cook and Hammack voted for an immediate hike, yet the 2-year yield eased to about 4.72% and the dollar index fell from a two-week high of about 102.4 to 102.15. Futures still price about 85% odds of a December hike, so the news was in the price.
BoC hikes, RBNZ and RBA diverge

The Bank of Canada raised rates for the first time since 2023, to 2.50%, and lifted its 2027 inflation forecast to 3.1%; USD/CAD fell about 0.4% to 1.3990. The RBNZ's surprise hold at 2.75% sank the kiwi about 1.7%, while hot Australian CPI pushed RBA hike odds for Nov 3 to about 88% and AUD/USD up 0.4% to 0.7055.
Oil back above $115 hits Asian importers

A Houthi missile strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery lifted Brent about 1.4% to near $115.4. The rupiah closed at a record 18,184 and the rupee lost 21 paise to about 95.28, while the won fell 14 to 1,337.7 even as the Kospi jumped 6.6%, as short covering and offshore hedging swamped equity inflows.
view: Mildly firmer over the next 1–2 weeks, but less one-way: the Fed leans hawkish and a December hike is about 85% priced, so the dollar needs hot PCE on Thursday to push higher. I back it against the euro, rupiah and peso, where energy, France and outflows weigh, but fade it against the loonie, yen and Taiwan dollar, where central banks are hiking or leaning against weakness. A DXY close below 101.70 or soft PCE would turn me neutral; a close above 102.80 would make me dollar-positive across the board.
ideas: Short from 1.4030–1.4050 (filled, about 0.4% in favour) after the BoC hike; for 1.3850, stop trailed to 1.4080.
Short from 157.50–157.80 (filled) into Friday's BoJ and Tokyo's warnings, for 155.00, stop 158.60, about 3:1.
Short from 32.53 (filled, about 0.35% in favour) as foreign Taiex buying returns; for 32.05, stop 32.65.
review: USD/CAD's short is about 0.4% in favour and USD/TWD's about 0.35%; USD/PHP's long from 63.50 is about 0.8% up and USD/IDR's about 1%; USD/JPY, EUR/USD and EUR/JPY shorts are roughly flat; USD/KRW's sell from 1,330–1,335 is about 0.3% against after a 14-won jump. AUD/USD and USD/CNH entries were missed as moves ran our way; ranges held. I trail the CAD, rupiah and TWD stops, cut the won target to 1,320 and raise the Aussie and lower the yuan entry zones.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.25% to 1.1155 after a post-Fed bounce from near 1.112; ECB fixing 1.1133.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. The euro spent Asia and Europe near 1.112, close to its weakest since April 2025, on French fiscal worries and Brent back above $115, then rose to about 1.1160 as the dollar slipped once Warsh spoke and the US curve steepened. Nothing in Europe improved: the euro is still down about 1.5% in October, the worst major.
eurusd.outlook: Bearish: I sell bounces into 1.1170–1.1190 for 1.1050. A hawkish ECB on Thursday that closes it above 1.1240 ends the call; a hot US PCE would speed the fall.
eurusd.watch: The ECB and US GDP/PCE (Oct 29), euro-area flash CPI (Oct 30) and French spreads.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.15% to 1.3327 after a 1½-week low; a dull Budget left sterling flat on the euro.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, BoE Nov 5 is the swing.

gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Chancellor Healey kept the fiscal rules and £15 billion of headroom, in line with a Reuters poll, so 10-year gilt yields slipped about 2bp to 5.32% and sterling barely reacted. It dipped to a 1½-week low before the Fed, then recovered with the euro as the dollar eased after Warsh's press conference.
gbpusd.outlook: Range 1.3280–1.3450, buying near the bottom: the Budget removed a risk and BoE hike pricing supports sterling. A close below 1.3280 turns me bearish; above 1.3450 bullish.
gbpusd.watch: US PCE (Oct 29), UK data and the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Up about 0.4% to 0.7055 on hot CPI; RBA hike odds near 88%.
audusd.why: The Aussie did the moving. Q3 CPI rose 1.3% q/q, annual September CPI hit 4.3% against 4.2% expected and the trimmed mean rose 1.0%, above the RBA's 0.8% path, while Governor Bullock blamed domestic capacity as well as energy. Markets lifted Nov 3 hike odds to about 88%, and the kiwi's slump after the RBNZ hold added cross buying.
audusd.outlook: Bullish: a hike to 4.85% next week widens the rate gap over the Fed, so I buy dips into 0.7020–0.7035 for 0.7130. A close below 0.6970, likely on an RBA hold or hot US PCE, ends the call.
audusd.watch: US PCE (Oct 29), China PMIs (Oct 31) and the RBA (Nov 3).

usdjpy.note: Flat near 157.79 after a post-Fed spike toward 158.50 faded; Tokyo's 160 line still 2 yen away.

view.call: Short from 157.50–157.80; BoJ Friday, Tokyo warns.

usdjpy.why: Both sides pulled. Two Fed dissents for a hike lifted the pair toward 158.50, near its 200-day average, but the dollar gave it back as US 2-year yields slipped and the curve steepened during Warsh's briefing. Japanese services inflation of 3.7% keeps a December BoJ hike in view, which limited yen selling ahead of Friday's meeting.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the short from 157.50–157.80, roughly flat, for 155.00: a BoJ outlook report that flags upside inflation risk and intervention threats near 159–160 cap the pair. A close above 158.60, likely on hot PCE, ends the call.
usdjpy.watch: US GDP/PCE (Oct 29), the BoJ and Ueda (Oct 30) and Tokyo's 159–160 line.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.15% to 0.8278 after failing again near 0.8300 resistance.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving. The pair tested two-week highs above 0.8300 before the Fed, then slipped as the dollar eased after the decision. Swiss ZEW expectations fell to a six-month low, but the franc ignored it; global stocks rising on the AI rally kept haven demand light.
usdchf.outlook: Range 0.8230–0.8330 with no edge. A close above 0.8330 opens 0.8400; a stock selloff or Middle East escalation would push it back toward 0.8230.
usdchf.watch: US PCE (Oct 29), risk sentiment, European spreads and Swiss CPI (early Nov).

usdcad.note: Down about 0.4% to 1.3990 after the BoC's first hike since 2023, to 2.50%.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hikes, Fed holds.

usdcad.why: The loonie did most of the moving. The Bank of Canada hiked 25bp to 2.50%, lifted its 2027 inflation forecast to 3.1% from 2.0% and said more may be needed, so Canada's 2-year yield hit 3.44%, its highest since August 2024. Oil up about 3% in WTI to near $102.8 helped, while the Fed's hold left the dollar softer.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.4% in favour, for 1.3850, trailing the stop to 1.4080: the rate gap keeps narrowing and markets fully price another BoC hike by January. A close above 1.4080, likely on US tariffs on Oct 30, ends the call.
usdcad.watch: US GDP/PCE (Oct 29), US tariffs on Canada (Oct 30), Canada GDP and oil.

usdcnh.note: Down about 0.1% to near 6.659; fixing 6.7165, still about 430 pips weaker than estimates.

view.call: Sell 6.665–6.675; PBOC lets the yuan grind up.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC held the pace steady. It set the midpoint at 6.7165, almost unchanged from Tuesday and about 430 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.6734, signalling it wants slow, not fast, gains. Onshore spot closed near 6.668 and the offshore yuan firmed late as the dollar eased after the Fed.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower: I sell 6.665–6.675 for 6.620. Fixings closer to estimates would speed it up; a close above 6.700 or a China stock selloff ends the call.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China PMIs (Oct 31) and US–China headlines.

usdhkd.note: Flat near 7.8452, still close to the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdhkd.why: Rate gaps keep it there. One-month HIBOR near 2.75% sits well below US rates on the Fed's 3.75–4.00% range, which the Fed just held, so borrowing Hong Kong dollars to hold US dollars still pays. There was no HKMA intervention, as the pair stayed just short of 7.85.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in the 7.83–7.85 band. A test of 7.85 would force HKMA buying and lift HIBOR; a dovish Fed would pull it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: HIBOR, HKMA action at 7.85 and US PCE (Oct 29).

usdsgd.note: Little changed near 1.2812, still just under 100-day average resistance near 1.2820.
usdsgd.why: The broad dollar set the tone. The Singapore dollar eased about 0.07% in Asia with the region as the dollar index hit a two-week high, then recovered as the dollar slipped after the Fed. A firm yuan and an S$NEER in the upper half of the MAS band keep moves small.
usdsgd.outlook: Range 1.2720–1.2830. A close above 1.2830 would open 1.2900; below 1.2720 reopens downside.
usdsgd.watch: US PCE (Oct 29), Singapore jobs data and the yuan.

usdkrw.note: Won fell 14.0 to 1,337.7 at the Seoul close despite a 6.6% Kospi jump; NDF near 1,342.
usdkrw.why: Positioning, not fundamentals, drove it. Once the pair broke out of the 1,320s, offshore funds bought dollars to hedge Korean stock holdings and onshore dealers covered dollar shorts, pushing it to 1,342.3. That swamped 816 billion won of foreign share buying as SK hynix's record results sent the Kospi up 6.6% to 6,012.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep selling into 1,335–1,342, but cut the target to 1,320: exporter supply and equity inflows should reassert once short covering ends. A close above 1,345 ends the call.
usdkrw.watch: Samsung's results, Korea's October exports (Nov 1), month-end flows and US PCE.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar rose 3.4 cents to 32.418, a 1-week high, as foreigners bought NT$15.9bn of shares.

view.call: Fade from 32.53; foreign buying, central bank.

usdtwd.why: Taiwan's own flows did the moving. The Taiex jumped about 2% to retake 47,000 on the AI rally, foreigners turned net buyers of about NT$15.9 billion and exporters sold dollars, offsetting a firm dollar in Asia. The central bank told lawmakers it sold about $17 billion this year to steady the currency, though the governor denied any fixed 32.50 line.
usdtwd.outlook: My fade from 32.53 is about 0.35% in favour; I extend the target to 32.05, near mid-October levels, and trail the stop to 32.65. Renewed foreign Taiex selling that closes it above 32.65 ends the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, US big-tech earnings, US PCE (Oct 29).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit firmed to 4.0745/0790 at the 6pm close from 4.0865/0900, gaining on most currencies.
usdmyr.why: Local confidence did the moving. Analysts cited AI-linked investment and steady growth, plus talk of eventual policy-rate normalisation, as the ringgit rose even with the dollar firm in Asia. As an oil exporter, Malaysia also gains when Brent rises, unlike its importing neighbours.
usdmyr.outlook: Range 4.06–4.10, now near the floor; I would not chase it lower before the Fed's message settles. A close below 4.06 would turn me bullish on the ringgit.
usdmyr.watch: US PCE (Oct 29), oil and Bank Negara (Nov 5).

usdphp.note: Peso rose 14.5 centavos to 64.025, ending a run of record lows, after a 64.18 intraday low.

view.call: Long; add 63.95–64.05. Oil, BoP gap swamp BSP.

usdphp.why: Position squaring before the Fed gave the peso a breather. It touched a new intraday record low of 64.18 at the open, then recovered to 64.025 on volume of about $1.66 billion. Oil back above $115 and a 1.9% drop in Philippine stocks show the pressure is intact, despite last week's surprise 50bp BSP hike to 5.50%.
usdphp.outlook: My long from 63.50 is about 0.8% in favour; I add on dips to 63.95–64.05 for 64.50. An Iran deal or heavy BSP dollar sales that close it below 63.80 end the call.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments, oil and Iran, US PCE (Oct 29) and US midterms (Nov 3).

usdidr.note: Rupiah fell 28 points to 18,184 (Bloomberg), past June's record close; JISDOR 18,183.
usdidr.why: Oil and outflows did the moving. Bank Indonesia blamed Middle East uncertainty that keeps oil above $115, rising US hike expectations and EM outflows, while foreign investors kept selling Jakarta stocks over MSCI's market-status review. The rupiah is down about 1.15% this month even as BI keeps intervening.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long from near 18,000, about 1% in favour, adding on dips to 18,120–18,150 for 18,300 and trailing the stop to 18,110. Heavy BI intervention or an MSCI fix that closes it below 18,110 ends the call.
usdidr.watch: MSCI's review, Jakarta flows, BI action at records, oil and US PCE (Oct 29).

usdinr.note: Rupee fell 21 paise to about 95.28 (provisional), near the day's low, as oil rose.

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI near the top, oil caps the rupee.

usdinr.why: Oil did the moving. Brent jumped back above $115 after the strike on a Saudi refinery, lifting importer dollar demand, while a firm dollar before the Fed and a 353-point Sensex drop added pressure. Likely RBI dollar sales and the special window for oil refiners kept the fall orderly.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.50–95.50: the RBI defends the top, while oil above $110 blocks a big rupee rally. A close above 95.50 would signal a new weaker leg.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran, RBI action, foreign flows and US PCE (Oct 29).

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.25% to near 176.0 as the euro bounced while the yen held flat.
eurjpy.why: The euro was the moving leg. It recovered with the post-Fed dip in the dollar while USD/JPY ended flat, so the cross rose to about 176.0 (EUR/USD 1.1155 × USD/JPY 157.79). Nothing changed the euro's drags: French bond worries and $115 oil.
eurjpy.outlook: My sell zone filled; I hold for 174.00 with the ECB and BoJ in back-to-back sessions. A close above 177.00, likely on a hawkish ECB, ends the call.
eurjpy.watch: The ECB (Oct 29), BoJ (Oct 30), French spreads and risk sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Edged up to near 23.70 as the yuan firmed and the yen held flat.
cnhjpy.why: The yuan was the moving leg. USD/CNH slipped about 0.1% while USD/JPY ended flat, so the cross edged up to about 23.70 (USD/JPY 157.79 ÷ USD/CNH 6.659), in the upper half of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range. A hawkish BoJ would push it toward 23.3; a break above 23.8 would need USD/JPY near 158.6.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: the ECB and US GDP/PCE (Oct 29), the BoJ and US tariffs on Canada (Oct 30), China PMIs (Oct 31), Korea exports (Nov 1), the RBA and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), plus oil, Tokyo's 159–160 line and records in the rupiah and peso.
sources: Reuters via Euronext (dollar after the Fed)
